henry.title: Edinburgh Castle: A Fortress That Was Attacked Again and Again
henry.intro: Edinburgh Castle sits on a rock in Scotland's capital city. Dad may see it on his trip! You'll read two pages from the castle's own website and be a history detective. (About 15 minutes.)
steps: FIRST (7 min): open link 1, 'History of the Castle'. Scroll to the parts called Ancient Stronghold and Royal Residence. Find answers to questions 1 to 4.
NEXT (4 min): open link 2, 'Family Day Out'. Scroll to Mons Meg. Answer question 6. (If a cookie box pops up, click 'Reject all and close'.)
LAST (4 min): put the years in order (question 5). Done when all 6 answers are written!
Word help: fortress = a strong castle for defense. siege = surrounding a place to capture it. sceptre = a royal stick. ramparts = castle walls.
links: Edinburgh Castle: History of the Castle
Read 'Ancient Stronghold' and 'Royal Residence' and look for the years.
Find 'Mons Meg' to see how far her cannonball could fly.
worksheet: Who built a hill fort on the castle rock long before the kings? ____________ people
In 1314 the Scots took back the castle in a night raid. Who led it? ____________
In 1715 a group tried to climb in. Why did it fail? (Hint: a ladder.) ____________
The Honours of Scotland are the crown, the ______ and the sword of state. They are the ______ (oldest / newest) crown jewels in Britain.
Order the events 1 to 4: ___ Honours first used together (1543) ___ Scots retake the castle (1314) ___ James VI is born in the Royal Palace (1566) ___ Mons Meg is given to King James II (1457)
Mons Meg's team of oxen could haul her 5 km a day. How many days to haul her 15 km? ___ days

frankie.title: Let's Build a Castle! 🏰
frankie.intro: Grown-up, read aloud: A big old castle in Scotland has tall towers, thick walls and a gate. Let's look at pictures, then draw one. (About 10 minutes.)
steps: Grown-up: open the link and look at the photos together (tap 'Reject all and close' on the cookie box). Find the big cannon and the tall walls.
Say: a castle has a ▭ square wall, a △ pointy roof and a ◯ round window. Count the towers or flags you see in the photos.
Frankie draws his castle and does the worksheet. Done!
links: Grown-up: scroll and look at the photos with Frankie. Find the cannon!
worksheet: Draw a castle using shapes: ▭ for the wall, △ for the roof, ◯ for a window.
